text: Course Title: Introduction to CSS Course Goal This course introduces beginners to CSS and shows how CSS is used to style HTML pages. By the end of the course, learners should understand the basic syntax of CSS, how to connect CSS to HTML, and how to apply simple styling to text, colors, spacing, and page layout. Target Audience Beginners with basic HTML knowledge. Learning Outcomes By the end of this course, learners will be able to: - Explain what CSS is and why it is important - Write basic CSS rules using selectors and declarations - Connect CSS to an HTML file - Change colors, fonts, sizes, and spacing - Use borders, backgrounds, and alignment - Apply simple box model concepts - Build a small styled web page Course Structure Lesson 1: What is CSS? - Definition of CSS - Difference between HTML and CSS - Why CSS is important in web development - Examples of unstyled and styled pages Lesson 2: CSS Syntax and Basic Rules - Selectors - Properties - Values - Rule structure - Writing simple CSS examples Lesson 3: Ways to Add CSS - Inline CSS - Internal CSS - External CSS - Why external CSS is usually preferred Lesson 4: Styling Text - Text color - Font size - Font family - Font weight - Text alignment - Line height Lesson 5: Colors and Backgrounds - Named colors - Hex colors - RGB colors - Background color - Background image basics Lesson 6: Borders, Margins, and Padding - Border basics - Margin basics - Padding basics - Difference between margin and padding Lesson 7: Introduction to the Box Model - Content - Padding - Border - Margin - How the box model affects layout Lesson 8: Simple Page Styling Practice - Styling a heading - Styling paragraphs - Styling buttons or links - Styling sections with background and spacing Final Mini Project Learners create a simple personal webpage using HTML and CSS with: - A title - A short introduction - Styled text - Colors and background - Spacing and borders Teaching Style - Beginner-friendly explanations - Short and clear examples - Simple practice tasks after major concepts - Focus on practical understanding rather than advanced theory Important Notes - Keep the course short and introductory - Do not go deep into advanced topics like Flexbox, Grid, animations, or responsive design - Use simple examples that are easy for beginners to understand - Keep the tone clear, supportive, and practical
